questions.stem: With reference to India's monetary policy framework, in the context of retail inflation recently crossing the RBI's upper tolerance limit, consider the following statements: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Reserve Bank of India's inflation target under the flexible inflation targeting framework is based on the Consumer Price Index (Combined), not the Wholesale Price Index.
The current tolerance band permits retail inflation to range between 2% and 6%, with 6% as the upper limit.
The six-member Monetary Policy Committee has a majority of four members appointed by the Government of India from outside the RBI.
If retail inflation remains outside the tolerance band for three consecutive quarters, the RBI Governor is statutorily required to resign.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: RBI's flexible inflation targeting under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act uses CPI (Combined) with a 2-6% band. Statement 3 is wrong since the MPC is evenly split 3-3 between RBI members and government appointees, not a four-member external majority. Statement 4 is wrong because missing the band for three consecutive quarters only triggers a report to the Government explaining reasons and remedial timelines, not a resignation.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Retail inflation hits 6.09% in October, crosses RBI's upper tolerance limit
questions.pyqLink: Tests RBI's flexible inflation targeting framework (Section 45ZA, RBI Act); cf. UPSC 2021 Prelims question on expansionary monetary policy actions.

questions.stem: With reference to global carbon emissions and India's climate commitments, in the context of a recent report projecting a rise in India's emissions even as global emissions fall, consider the following statements: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Global Carbon Budget report referenced in the news is published annually by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) as part of its Assessment Report cycle.
China remains the world's largest emitter of carbon dioxide in absolute terms, followed by the United States and India.
India's updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) under the Paris Agreement targets a 45% reduction in the emissions intensity of its GDP by 2030 compared to the 2005 level.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Global Carbon Budget is produced by the Global Carbon Project, an independent research consortium, not the IPCC's Assessment Report process. Statement 2 is correct, as China, the US and India are consistently the top three absolute emitters in that order. Statement 3 is correct, reflecting India's 2022-updated NDC commitment to cut GDP emissions intensity 45% from 2005 levels by 2030.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Global carbon emissions are set to fall. Why are India’s emissions projected to rise?
questions.pyqLink: Tests Global Carbon Project vs IPCC and India's NDC targets; cf. UPSC 2022 Prelims on the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change.

questions.stem: With reference to the institutional framework for insolvency resolution in India, in the context of the National Company Law Tribunal declaring a corporate promoter personally bankrupt over a loan guarantee, consider the following two statements: Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
statements: Statement-I: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) is the adjudicating authority under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 for insolvency and bankruptcy proceedings against individuals who have furnished personal guarantees to corporate debtors.

Statement-II: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 could be enacted only after a Constitutional Amendment inserted a new entry on insolvency and bankruptcy into the Union List of the Seventh Schedule.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct: Section 60 read with Part III of the IBC makes NCLT the adjudicating authority for personal guarantors to corporate debtors, which is how NCLT could declare the Videocon promoter bankrupt. Statement-II is incorrect because 'insolvency and bankruptcy' has been Entry 9 of the Union List since the Constitution's commencement; no constitutional amendment was needed for Parliament to enact the IBC.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Videocon and the Venugopal Dhoot case: What happens when a person is declared bankrupt
questions.pyqLink: Tests NCLT's adjudicating role under the IBC, 2016 and the Union List entry on insolvency; cf. UPSC 2021 Prelims on Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code provisions.

questions.stem: A wearable health device has drawn scrutiny over its claim to track blood flow using a technology called Photoplethysmography (PPG). With reference to this technology, which one of the following best describes it?
options: It is an optical technique that detects blood volume changes in the microvascular bed of tissue by measuring variations in light absorption and reflection at the skin surface.
It is an electrical technique that records the heart's rhythm by measuring voltage differences generated by cardiac muscle depolarization through electrodes placed on the skin.
It is an ultrasound-based imaging technique that uses high-frequency sound waves to visualize blood flow velocity within deep-seated arteries such as the carotid artery.
It is a radiological imaging technique that uses ionizing radiation to generate cross-sectional images of soft tissue and blood vessels.
questions.explanation: PPG is an optical sensing method: it shines light into the skin and measures how much is absorbed or reflected as blood volume changes with each heartbeat, which is exactly why doctors in the article questioned whether it could distinguish brain blood flow from superficial scalp circulation. Option 2 describes an ECG, option 3 describes Doppler ultrasound, and option 4 describes a CT scan — none of which is the technology used in the wearable.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Deepinder Goyal's Temple: Can a wearable really measure blood flow inside your brain?
questions.pyqLink: Tests identification of biomedical sensing technologies by principle; analogous to UPSC's recurring science-tech term-identification questions (e.g., UPSC 2019 on Merchant Discount Rate-style definitional MCQs).

questions.stem: A new 'Total Chess' tournament format has renewed interest in the game's origins. With reference to the history of chess, consider the following statements: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Chess is widely believed to have originated in India, evolving from an ancient strategy game known as Chaturanga.
The term 'Chaturanga' derives from a Sanskrit word referring to the four divisions of an ancient Indian army — infantry, cavalry, elephantry and chariotry.
From India, the game is believed to have spread to Persia, where it was known as Shatranj, before reaching the Arab world and subsequently Europe.
The term 'checkmate', used across modern chess, is derived from the Persian phrase 'Shah Mat', meaning roughly 'the king is helpless'.
questions.explanation: All four statements reflect the established account of chess's Indian origins and westward transmission: Chaturanga's four-fold army divisions, its evolution into Persian Shatranj, its further spread via the Arab world into Europe, and the English 'checkmate' preserving the Persian 'Shah Mat'. None of the statements is factually incorrect.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Total Chess, explained: Inside the made-for-TV tournament reimagining the sport
questions.pyqLink: Tests the ancient Indian origins of chess (Chaturanga) under History, Art and Culture; similar in style to UPSC Prelims questions on games/sports of ancient Indian origin.

questions.stem: Andhra Pradesh hosted a major investor summit at Visakhapatnam. With reference to major seaports of India, consider the following pairs of ports and the type of harbour they possess: How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Visakhapatnam, set amid hill promontories on the east coast, and Paradip, near the Mahanadi delta, are genuine natural harbours, and Kandla (Deendayal Port) on the Gulf of Kutch is correctly classed as a tidal port since vessel movement there is governed by tidal variation. Chennai is wrongly matched — it required artificial breakwaters and is classified as a man-made harbour, not a natural one.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: 'New state law to shield investors in Andhra Pradesh'
questions.pyqLink: Tests natural vs artificial/tidal harbours among major Indian ports; cf. UPSC Prelims questions on major seaports of India.

questions.stem: The West Asia conflict has pushed up crude and jet fuel prices, feeding into India's inflation. With reference to India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves, consider the following statements: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves are stored in underground rock caverns at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur, and are maintained separately from the buffer stocks held by public sector oil marketing companies.
These strategic reserves are intended primarily to meet defence requirements during war and are maintained by the Ministry of Defence.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the underground rock-cavern reserves at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur are run by the Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Limited (ISPRL) under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, distinct from the working/buffer stocks of OMCs like IOC and BPCL. Statement 2 is incorrect because the reserves exist to cushion the economy against global crude-supply disruptions and price shocks, not for defence purposes, and fall under the petroleum ministry rather than defence.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Flight tickets, food and more: 5 charts that explain what’s driving inflation higher, wider
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's Strategic Petroleum Reserve locations and administering body amid West Asia supply-shock context; cf. UPSC 2021 Prelims question on Strategic Petroleum Reserves of India.

questions.stem: With reference to the legal basis for action against an Air Force officer accused of passing classified information to a foreign operative, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: The disclosure of classified military information to a foreign agent is punishable as an offence under the Official Secrets Act, 1923.

Statement-II: The Official Secrets Act, 1923 is a pre-constitutional statute that continues to operate as the principal law governing espionage and protection of official secrets in India, and the restrictions it imposes fall within the 'security of the State' ground permitted under Article 19(2) of the Constitution.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: The Official Secrets Act, 1923, enacted before Independence and continued under Article 372, is the primary statute criminalising spying and unauthorised disclosure of secret information; it derives constitutional validity from the 'security of the State' restriction under Article 19(2), which explains why such disclosures remain punishable today. Neither statement is incorrect, and Statement-II directly accounts for why Statement-I holds true.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: IAF officer shared war plans, deployment details with Pak operative: Police to court
questions.pyqLink: Tests Official Secrets Act 1923 and Article 19(2) reasonable restrictions, a recurring polity theme (cf. UPSC questions on fundamental rights restrictions).

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the pricing of petrol and diesel in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Prices of petrol and diesel were deregulated and linked to international crude prices and market dynamics, petrol in 2010 and diesel in 2014.
The Union Government directly subsidises Oil Marketing Companies from the Consolidated Fund of India whenever retail diesel prices are not raised in line with rising crude oil costs.
Central excise duty on petrol and diesel is a specific (fixed per-litre) duty and does not change automatically with fluctuations in crude oil prices.
The Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell functions under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and monitors international oil prices and domestic consumption trends.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct: petrol was deregulated in June 2010 and diesel in October 2014; excise duty is a specific duty requiring explicit notification to change; and PPAC sits under the Petroleum Ministry tracking prices and consumption. Statement 2 is incorrect — post-deregulation, there is no automatic budgetary subsidy to OMCs from the Consolidated Fund; under-recoveries, where they occur, are largely absorbed by the OMCs themselves or offset through excise/tax adjustments, not direct subsidy.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: PM Modi: In farmer interest, Government hiked diesel price by just Rs 7, not Rs 50
questions.pyqLink: Tests administered pricing mechanism and petroleum subsidy architecture, close to UPSC's recurring questions on oil subsidy and under-recovery.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of forest-related laws and the provisions associated with them:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Requires prior approval of the Central Government for diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes
Lays down the procedure for diversion of forest land to non-forest use by State Governments
Establishes funds to utilise compensatory afforestation and net present value payments collected from user agencies
Empowers State Governments to declare forest areas as Reserved, Protected or Village Forests
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is incorrect: the procedure for diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes is laid down under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, not the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, which instead governs protected areas and species protection — the kind of unauthorised forest-land use for non-forest installations that the Assam case (commando camps on forest land) implicates.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Assam: Retired forest officer on repeated extensions to be put in mines department now
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 clearance mechanism versus the Wildlife Protection Act, a frequent static-current fusion area in UPSC.

questions.stem: With reference to quantum computing, which one of the following best describes a 'trapped-ion' qubit system, the technology for which an Infosys Prize 2026 winner was recognised?
options: It uses superconducting loops cooled close to absolute zero to form qubits, with microwave pulses used for gate operations
It uses individual charged atoms held in place by electromagnetic fields in a vacuum, with their internal energy states manipulated by lasers to perform quantum logic operations
It uses photons as qubits transmitted through optical fibre networks primarily for quantum key distribution
It uses the spin states of electrons in silicon-based semiconductor quantum dots at cryogenic temperatures
questions.explanation: Trapped-ion quantum computing confines individual ions using electromagnetic (Paul or Penning) traps in a vacuum and manipulates their internal quantum states with laser pulses to implement qubits and logic gates. Option (a) describes superconducting-qubit systems (e.g., IBM, Google), option (c) describes photonic/QKD systems, and option (d) describes silicon spin-qubit systems — all distinct competing quantum-computing architectures.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Six, including quantum and climate change researchers, win Infosys Prize
questions.pyqLink: Tests distinction between quantum computing architectures (trapped-ion vs superconducting vs photonic vs spin qubits), an emerging Sci-Tech theme.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about Wazwan, the traditional Kashmiri feast in the news recently:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Wazwan is a traditional multi-course non-vegetarian meal associated with Kashmiri wedding feasts, prepared predominantly by hereditary chefs called Wazas.
The Wazwan culinary tradition traces much of its technique and dishes to Persian and Central Asian influences introduced during the Mughal and pre-Mughal period in Kashmir.
Wazwan has been formally inscribed by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Wazwan is prepared by hereditary Waza chefs for Kashmiri weddings and its multi-course format and dishes reflect Persian and Central Asian culinary influences absorbed over centuries. Statement 3 is incorrect — Wazwan has not been inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage, though it is often discussed as a candidate for such recognition.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: No meal after 10 pm: Kashmiri wedding chefs have had enough of late-night feasts
questions.pyqLink: Tests awareness of regional cultural/culinary heritage and the distinction from actual UNESCO ICH inscriptions, similar to past questions on India's UNESCO-listed intangible heritage items.

questions.stem: With reference to the Siang River, around whose upper multipurpose hydro project protests have continued in Arunachal Pradesh, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Siang River is the name given to the Brahmaputra as it flows through Arunachal Pradesh after entering India from Tibet, where it is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo.
The Siang Upper Multipurpose Project is being developed primarily to divert the river's water for irrigation in the Brahmaputra Valley of Assam.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet becomes the Siang on entering Arunachal Pradesh and later the Brahmaputra in Assam. Statement 2 is incorrect: the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project is primarily a hydropower project, often framed as a strategic response to Chinese dam-building upstream, not an irrigation-diversion scheme.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Out after month in detention, Siang activist Adum Tayong says stir will continue
questions.pyqLink: Tests river-naming and course of the Brahmaputra system across Tibet-India, a recurring physical geography theme.

questions.stem: Ahead of PM Modi's visit to Manila for the ASEAN-India and East Asia Summits, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The ASEAN-India Summit is held annually and brings together India with the ten member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.
The East Asia Summit, in which India participates, includes all ten ASEAN member states along with India, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, Russia and the United States.
The chairmanship of the East Asia Summit rotates independently of the ASEAN chairmanship and is held by a different member state each year.
India's 'Act East Policy' forms the diplomatic framework guiding its engagement with ASEAN and the wider East Asia Summit process.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: the ASEAN-India Summit is an annual ten-plus-one format, the East Asia Summit comprises the ten ASEAN states plus eight dialogue partners including India, and the Act East Policy (successor to the Look East Policy) guides India's engagement with both. Statement 3 is incorrect — the East Asia Summit chairmanship coincides with whichever country holds the ASEAN chair that year (the Philippines in 2026), it does not rotate independently.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: India news Live Updates, 13 November 2026: Severe air quality grips Delhi as AIIMS AQI hits 418
questions.pyqLink: Tests composition and chairmanship mechanics of ASEAN-India Summit and East Asia Summit, a regularly tested IR grouping.

questions.stem: An eight-year-old child recently underwent a Peroral Endoscopic Myotomy for Type II Achalasia, a disorder that impairs swallowing. With reference to Achalasia, which one of the following best describes this condition?
options: It is a bacterial infection of the oesophagus causing ulceration and painful swallowing, treated primarily with antibiotics.
It is a disorder in which the lower oesophageal sphincter fails to relax adequately, impairing the passage of food and liquid into the stomach.
It is a condition in which stomach acid flows back into the oesophagus, producing a burning sensation commonly known as heartburn.
It is a genetic disorder of the taste buds that leads to loss of appetite and consequent difficulty in swallowing.
questions.explanation: The article states Achalasia affects the nerves controlling oesophageal muscles, causing the lower oesophageal sphincter to remain abnormally tight and blocking normal passage of food/liquid into the stomach, which matches option B exactly. Option A describes infective oesophagitis, option C describes GERD (a distinct disorder), and option D is fictitious.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Eight-year-old undergoes endoscopic treatment for rare swallowing disorder
questions.pyqLink: Tests static human physiology/digestive system concept; similar in style to UPSC's term-definition questions (e.g., 2020 TB-cure statement set).

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the newly identified Indian Bramble Shark (Echinorhinus roinee). How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The species was identified through research conducted jointly by the Zoological Survey of India and the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute.
The species inhabits shallow coastal waters at depths of less than 50 metres.
The Zoological Survey of India functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
The ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute operates under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research, which functions under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct: the discovery was a joint ZSI-CMFRI effort, ZSI is under MoEFCC, and CMFRI is an ICAR institute under the Agriculture Ministry. Statement 2 is false — the article specifies the shark lives along continental slopes at depths of 350 to 450 metres, not shallow coastal waters.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: New shark species identified in Indian Ocean after decades of misclassification
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional affiliation of science bodies and marine biodiversity/habitat facts, a recurring UPSC pairs/statement theme (e.g., 2023 pairs-matched questions on research institutions).

questions.stem: With reference to climate finance negotiations under the UNFCCC, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The New Collective Quantified Goal of mobilising USD 300 billion annually by 2035 for climate finance was decided at COP29 held in Baku.
The global stocktake under the Paris Agreement is a one-time exercise conducted only in the year the Agreement entered into force.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the editorial confirms the $300 billion/year by 2035 goal was decided at COP29 in Baku. Statement 2 is incorrect because the global stocktake is a periodic exercise conducted every five years under the Paris Agreement, not a one-time event; the article itself refers to the 'second' global stocktake beginning at COP31.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Paris Agreement's global stocktake mechanism and COP finance goals, similar to UPSC's recurring UNFCCC/COP institutional questions.

questions.stem: South Korea recently required Google to remove coordinates of sensitive sites from its maps under an export permit condition. With reference to India's geospatial data policy, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Guidelines for Acquisition and Production of Geospatial Data, 2021 removed the requirement of prior permission or license before acquiring geospatial data of Indian territory.

Indian geospatial policy requires mapping agencies to exclude or restrict high-resolution imagery of notified strategic and military installations through a negative list maintained by the government.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The 2021 Guidelines liberalised India's geospatial sector by replacing the earlier prior-approval regime with self-certification, and the policy separately maintains restrictions (a negative list) on imaging/mapping around sensitive military and strategic installations — conceptually the same safeguard South Korea invoked against Google.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: South Korea says Google has removed Korean coordinates from maps under export permit
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's geospatial/mapping policy framework, an emerging static topic linked to remote sensing and national security in the Geography/Science & Technology syllabus.

questions.stem: In the context of the economics of hyperscale AI data centres being built in India, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Data centres were accorded 'infrastructure' status in India under the Harmonised Master List of Infrastructure Sub-sectors in 2022.
100% Foreign Direct Investment is permitted in the data centre sector in India through the automatic route.
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has formally notified a National Data Centre Policy granting Special Economic Zone-like incentives to data centre parks.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: data centres were added to the Harmonised Master List of Infrastructure Sub-sectors in 2022, and 100% FDI is allowed under the automatic route for the sector. Statement 3 is incorrect because the National Data Centre Policy has remained in draft form since 2020 and has not been formally notified.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Age of AI: behind Tarluvada's blue wall in Visakhapatnam
questions.pyqLink: Tests infrastructure-status classification and FDI policy, a recurring theme in UPSC economy questions on the Harmonised Master List and FDI limits across sectors.

questions.stem: The discovery of a new shark species involved India's premier scientific survey institutions. Consider the following pairs of organisations and their administrative/parent ministry. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
questions.explanation: Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched: ZSI is an attached office of the MoEFCC, and CMFRI (an ICAR institute) falls under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. Pair 3 is wrong because the Wildlife Institute of India also functions under MoEFCC, not the Ministry of Earth Sciences. Pair 4 is wrong because the Botanical Survey of India is likewise under MoEFCC, not the Ministry of Culture.

questions.sourceTitle: New shark species identified in Indian Ocean after decades of misclassification
